neighbours.label: the verb of a company's formal undertaking or disclaimer in terms and notices (We make no warranty; will use reasonable efforts; We take all reasonable steps)
fire: The publisher makes no representation regarding the completeness of these figures.
Acme Ltd will use all reasonable endeavours to dispatch orders within 48 hours.
Our company takes reasonable precautions to protect your personal data.
The seller makes no guarantee that the item will suit any particular purpose.
The provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to restore the service.
The hotel accepts no liability for valuables left in guest rooms.
Northwind gives no warranty, express or implied, about this software.
The organiser will take every reasonable step to ensure the event runs on time.
quiet: The publisher printed the new figures on the back page of the report.
Acme Ltd opened a second warehouse near the harbour last spring.
Our company hired twelve engineers for the new data team.
The seller wrapped the item carefully and posted it on Tuesday.
The provider moved its offices to a larger building downtown.
The hotel has a rooftop pool and a small garden for guests.
Northwind released a new version of the software in March.
The organiser booked a band and a caterer for the evening.

notes: Top examples are all legal/terms boilerplate. Probe: casual 'use the pen' is quiet, but casual 'make pancakes' fired as much as 'make no warranty', so ' make' itself may carry it; near misses avoid make.
